text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Russian customs agents have held 26 Estonian trucks near Moscow for the past two weeks without explaining why. The drivers have appealed to the Estonian embassy.
- The government decided not to convene parliament in August for an extra session in order to discuss customs tarriffs.
- The government intends to raise the fuel excise by 50 cents every year in order to reach western European price levels by the year 2000.
- The traffic police have complained about commercial radio stations warning motorists about police checks. The press council will decide later this month on the ethical aspects of the situation.
- The interior ministry wants to inroduce a national emergency number.
- The defence ministry will buy apartments for 150 officers for ten million kroons.
- The owners of the Estonian Investment Bank want to sell it to foreign buyers.
- Forekspank has been criticised for its failure to inform the stock exchange about the freezing of its corresponding accounts in Russia two weeks ago.
